7739.evidence: Champ cars used turbocharged engines that ran on methanol fuel. Cosworth (later branded as the Ford-Cosworth), Ilmor (branded as Chevrolet), and Buick engines were common powerplants through the mid-1990s. By the 1990s, engines were typically leased from manufacturers, who conducted research and development during the racing season; one engine could easily dominate competition in the first part of the season and then fall behind.
